title: lava features --json
description: Feature flags. Bare, it lists every flag with the layer that decided it; with a name, it resolves that one and reports the full trace — code default, then each layer that overrode it, in order. The trace is the point: 'why is this on?' is answered by the layers, not by the final value, and a flag's answer can differ per subject, which is why the resolver is deterministic and stateless.

data.description: Two shapes: the list, and one flag's resolution. They are distinguishable by key, and each forbids the other's, so a consumer can branch on `features` vs `flag` alone.

setting.description: A flag setting as written: on, off, rollout:N (deterministic bucketing), users:id,id, or env:NAME (read from the environment at resolution time).

layer.description: One layer of the resolution, in the order it was applied.
code = the default in config/features.php's define block; config = that file's set block or an environment branch; env = LAVA_FEATURE_* in the real environment.

features.description: Every defined flag, in declaration order.

pack.description: The pack that defined it, or null for an app-defined flag.

enabled.description: The answer for the resolved environment with no subject — an audience flag is off for anonymous subjects.

decided_by.description: The outermost layer that decided it.

flag.description: The flag's resolution. Null when the invocation was refused before a flag was named — a usage error still carries this key, so the shape is a resolution in which nothing was resolved. Without the null, the refused envelope matches neither branch of the `oneOf` above and fails its own schema.

trace.description: Every layer that applied, innermost first — the whole answer to 'why is it on', not just the winner.

subject.description: The subject this was resolved for (--subject), or null for the anonymous default.
